correctness.rationale: The multiplier theorem is correct. Under |b_1|<=2 and the area theorem, condition (A) is exactly the support function of the product of the b_1 disk and weighted Hilbert tail, giving |Q_c(z)-1|<1 for every |z|<1 even at boundary equality. The identity U_F=Q_c-zQ_c'-1=-sum_{n>=2}(n-1)c_n b_n z^n plus condition (B) gives the strict U-class bound. For c_n=(n+1)^(-sigma), (A) yields the unique threshold equation and (B) is safely automatic at sigma>1.4.

originality.rationale: The complete 2013 source was inspected: its Corollary 1.7 states the coarser universal sigma>=3/2 conclusion and the paper explicitly asks for the smallest parameter. Its proof uses the same broad coefficient inputs but introduces a coarser tail estimate. The filed exact Hilbert support-function formulation and resulting 1.4135195... upper endpoint were not found there or in the checked related transform papers. The claim is appropriately limited to the relaxed coefficient body; it does not pretend that the Hilbert extremal is necessarily a schlicht coefficient sequence.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem identifies the exact limitation of a natural Bieberbach-plus-area-theorem absolute-value method and simultaneously improves a published open-problem bound. The general multiplier criterion is reusable beyond the one polylogarithmic kernel.

citations.note: Ali, Obradović and Ponnusamy (2013), complete primary source; gives the sigma>=3/2 corollary and asks for the smallest parameter.
Obradović, Ponnusamy and Vasundhra (2009), related nonlinear integral transforms with more restrictive input classes.

findings: Condition (A) is exactly the relaxed coefficient-body support function, not merely another Cauchy–Schwarz upper bound.
Strict inequality in the disk follows from the r^n factors even when the boundary norm equals one.
For the polylog multipliers, the same root s_*=1.413519504254766... is obtained.
The source’s 3/2 theorem and open problem were verified directly in the complete 2013 paper.
independent_checks: Re-derived both Cauchy–Schwarz estimates and the support-function equality.
Checked the automatic condition-(B) tail bound in the claimed sigma range.
Verified uniqueness/monotonicity of the threshold equation and recomputed its root.
Inspected the complete 2013 paper, including the stated corollary and terminal open problem.
limitations: The true universal threshold remains unknown; this is an improved sufficient bound.
Support-function sharpness is only for the relaxed Bieberbach-area coefficient body, not the exact schlicht coefficient body.
An equivalent older multiplier theorem under different notation remains a residual literature risk.
record_title: An exact area-theorem Hilbert envelope lowers a polylogarithmic reciprocal univalence threshold
